title: ConfigureAwait(false)
sub: Skipping the context, and when that's dangerous
cards/0/title: Don't go back to the context
cards/0/body:
ConfigureAwait(false) tells await: "don't capture the SynchronizationContext". The continuation won't go via Post to the UI thread's queue; it runs on a pool thread instead. ExecutionContext is unaffected: AsyncLocal and culture flow as usual.

For library code that doesn't need the UI thread this is the right call: fewer switches, and no deadlock if someone outside calls .Result. Step by step, with an outer .Result in WPF:

  • 1. await doesn't capture the context, and the UI thread blocks on .Result.
  • 2. The response arrives, and a pool thread runs the continuation.
  • 3. The task completes without the UI thread.
  • 4. .Result on the UI thread gets the result. The UI thread itself was stuck the whole time.
cards/1/task: The code with .Result hangs. Fix it inside the library without touching the handler.
cards/2/q: WPF: the handler calls GetDataAsync().Result, and ConfigureAwait(false) was added to the await in the library. The deadlock is gone. What changed?
cards/2/options/0: A pool thread ran the continuation, and the task completed without the UI thread
cards/2/options/1: The UI thread stopped blocking on .Result
cards/2/explain: The UI thread was still stuck on .Result, but the task no longer needed it.
cards/3/task: Now the method updates a window control after await. What happens with ConfigureAwait(false)?
cards/4/q: WPF: after await http.GetStringAsync(url).ConfigureAwait(false) the method writes label.Text = json. Why does it throw?
cards/4/options/0: After ConfigureAwait(false) the code ran on a pool thread, and controls can only be touched from the UI thread
cards/4/explain: ConfigureAwait(false) only fits where you don't need the UI thread after the await.
cards/5/body:
In libraries, ConfigureAwait(false) on every await. In app code that touches the UI or the Unity API after await, leave it out.

But ConfigureAwait is a safety net, not a cure. The thread on .Result is still stuck. The real cure for the deadlock is not to block at all: next lesson.
cards/5/deep: .NET 8 added ConfigureAwaitOptions: for example, await task.ConfigureAwait(ConfigureAwaitOptions.SuppressThrowing) waits for the task without throwing. SuppressThrowing is supported only for a Task with no result: for Task<T> it's an error (the CA2261 analyzer, and ArgumentOutOfRangeException at run time). ASP.NET Core has no context, so there ConfigureAwait(false) changes nothing in app code.
cards/6/q: Where does ConfigureAwait(false) belong? Select all that apply.
cards/6/options/2: In a button handler that then changes label.Text
cards/6/options/3: In a Unity script that then moves a transform
cards/6/explain: Where the code touches the UI or the Unity API after await, it needs the main thread's context.
cards/7/title: ConfigureAwait only matters on a pause
cards/7/body:
ConfigureAwait(false) only decides where to send the continuation after a pause. If the task has already completed (a cache hit, the fast path), await doesn't stop, and the code keeps going on the same thread, which is still the UI thread.

The next await without ConfigureAwait(false) reads SynchronizationContext.Current again, captures the UI context, and the deadlock with an outer .Result is back. That's why ConfigureAwait(false) goes on every await, not just "at the start of the method".
cards/7/code:
var a = await cache.GetAsync(k).ConfigureAwait(false); // cache hit: still the UI thread
var b = await http.GetStringAsync(url);                // captures the UI context → deadlock risk
cards/8/q: In a library, ConfigureAwait(false) is only on the method's first await, not on the second. Outside, the method is called via .Result from the UI thread. What's the risk?
cards/8/options/0: If the first task completed right away, the code stayed on the UI thread, and the second await captures the UI context again
cards/8/options/1: None: after the first ConfigureAwait(false) the method is already running on the pool
cards/8/explain: Without a pause ConfigureAwait(false) has no effect: the thread doesn't change, and the second await sees the UI context.
cards/9/q: Does ConfigureAwait(false) stop AsyncLocal from flowing?
cards/9/options/0: No: it's about SynchronizationContext, while ExecutionContext always flows
cards/9/options/1: Yes: without the context AsyncLocal is lost
cards/9/explain: These are two independent mechanisms: SynchronizationContext decides who runs the continuation, ExecutionContext decides what data rides with it.
